questions.q: How does the capital market primarily benefit the government in national economic management?
options: By enabling the continuous printing of paper currency to clear recurring national budget deficits
By providing a structured platform to float long-term bonds to finance major public infrastructure without triggering inflationary pressures
By enforcing statutory price caps on consumer goods and retail commodities across the country
By taking over the day-to-day administrative running of non-performing public corporations
questions.explain: The capital market enables federal, state, and local governments to raise non-inflationary, long-term loan capital through the issuance of **development bonds** (e.g., FGN Bonds, Sukuk, Green Bonds). This long-term borrowing finances capital infrastructure (roads, bridges, dams, energy) without forcing the Central Bank to resort to inflationary deficit financing (printing money).
